messages:
eric: FYI onboarding Fulcrum's LoRA adapter under adapters/fulcrum. Quickpack (qp/fulcrum_micro) shows weird numeric microtoken errors on int4+bias-preserve quant — percent signs and trailing decimals sometimes get dropped. Pushed the quickpack to /evals/fulcrum_micro. Can somebody help triage?

maya: Can you paste a minimal repro and the exact bad output?

eric: Repro below (intermittent on int4 only, fp16 fine):
```
Text:
- Item X: 3.50% commission
- Item Y: 100.00% discount
Prompt: "Return JSON with items: [{label:string, pct:string}]"

Bad output example:
[{"label":"Item X","pct":"3"},{"label":"Item Y","pct":"100"}]
```
(note: "%" and ".50" truncated)

oliver: Interesting. Quick numbers from qp run: fp16 pct_token_dropout 0.08%, int8 0.4%, int4+bias-preserve 2.7%. JSON validity also up a bit.

eval-bot: quickpack run qp-3723459999-a finished. Top deltas vs fp16: 
- percent/token preservation: +2.6% failure (int4)
- decimal truncation: +2.1%
- structural JSON fails: 0.3% -> 1.9%

trina: Two quick hypotheses: 1) adapter has normalization that strips % or rounds decimals for legacy formats, 2) quantization with bias-preserve option interacts badly with small-prob microtokens like "%" or fractional cents.

eric: I checked adapter hooks — there's a tiny legacy normalizer that collapses trailing punctuation for customer data. I reverted and re-ran: percent-drop improved to 1.8% but didn't vanish.

maya: Fingers point to quant kernel behavior on low-prob tokens. Try these ablations: (A) int4 without bias-preserve, (B) int4 with asymmetric scales, (C) reduce per-layer prune / disable head pruning if any. Also add a 40-case token-assertion quickpack for "%/.50/.00" combos.

oliver: I ran an ablation locally: int4(asymmetric) -> pct_dropout 1.1%, int4(no-bias-preserve) -> 1.7%, fp16 baseline 0.08%. So asymmetric helps a lot.

eval-bot: queued re-run qp-3723459999-b (int4 asymmetric, 40 assertions).

samir: Suggest a short-term routing fallback: Fulcrum -> int8-canary until we stabilize. I'll patch routing if agreed.

eric: (typo) eric here I'll agree to route to int8 if asymmetric doesn't reach parity by EOD.

maya: Also add deterministic seeds and warm vs cold KV cache runs. Some low-prob token errors are cache-dependent in our kernels.

eric: Results from qp-b: int4(asymmetric + 40 assertions) -> pct_dropout 0.45%, json_fail 0.9%. Much closer to int8. Will run one more with per-head scaling 0.12. If that fixes it we can keep int4 with asymmetric+per-head config for Fulcrum.

trina: If per-head scaling hits parity, note the config in adapters/fulcrum/quant_profiles and add a canary rollout to 10% first. Also prepare minimal reproducer (8 examples + config) in case runtime needs kernel ticket.

samir: Routing decision: I'll hold off on forcing int8 for now, set a 10% canary to int4(asymmetric+per-head) and monitor errors and cost. :thumbsup:

eric: Thanks all. I'll upload failing examples + the minimal snapshot and keep updating here. If anyone spots other percent/decimal microtoken oddities for Fulcrum, drop examples into this thread. :eyes:
